raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, an active request can retain GPU-only pages
with null host entries when no host page is available. Later allocations extend
the host table, so freeing host capacity does not give those old pages backing
and their GPU blocks stay pinned.

Retry one old page per connector step after scheduler allocations. The recovered
page gets a host destination and a copy to host. Its GPU blocks become reclaimable
only after every worker completes the transfer.

In the 64-token regression case, releasing one donor host block lets the active
request backfill logical page 1. Completion makes **one GPU block per resident
group reclaimable**; partial acknowledgement makes none.

## Test coverage

`test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_keeps_gpu_pages_readable`
(`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:855`) fails on the baseline because the
old host entry remains null.

| Reviewer question | Test |
|---|---|
| Can retries duplicate work or monopolize capacity? | `test_hisparse_host_recovery_rotates_requests_with_limited_capacity` (`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:939`) |
| Can a late completion validate a reused request ID? | `test_hisparse_host_recovery_retains_cancelled_transfer_endpoints` (`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:981`) |
| Does eager mirroring copy the recovered page? | `test_host_recovery_copies_pages_even_with_eager_mirroring` (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) |

AI assistance from Codex was used for the implementation, tests, and this
description.

## Validation

The CPU run completed with **205 passed**:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q --tb=short
```

The H100 model-path regression completed with **2 passed** (eager host mirroring
on and off):

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -k host_capacity_recovery -v -s -x --tb=short
```

Each H100 case copied 3 recovered pages, reclaimed 24 GPU blocks across 8
resident groups, and preserved all 16 generated tokens with zero preemptions.
Host rows matched resident rows. The run used reduced DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy
FP8 weights, so trained-model accuracy was not evaluated. Serving throughput
was not measured.

## Existing PRs

Open PR searches for HiSparse host capacity recovery, exhaustion, and backfill
found no implementation of recovery for old null host entries. #56109 addresses
resident cache policy and does not backfill these entries.

nodes.body: Thanks for the PR! I think the better approach is to mandate host backing, though, as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59036 does. I'm going to go with that PR and close this one

     # Host publication and spills

+    def record_missing_host_pages(self, request_id: str, pages: range) -> None:
+        if not pages or not self.resident_managers:
+            return
+        self._get_request_state(request_id).missing_host_pages.extend(pages)
+        self._host_recovery_requests[request_id] = None
+
+    def recover_host_page(self) -> int | None:
+        """Retry one queued page after the step's mandatory host allocations.
+
+        Rotate requests after each attempt to bound both lookup work and added
+        DMA to one page per step, including requests with an unsealed tail.
+        """
+        if (
+            not self._host_recovery_requests
+            or len(self.spills_to_send) >= self.max_spill_pages
+        ):
+            return None
+        assert self.host_manager is not None
+        pool = self.host_manager.block_pool
+        if not pool.get_num_free_blocks():
+            return None
+        request_id = next(iter(self._host_recovery_requests))
+        self._host_recovery_requests.move_to_end(request_id)

+            return None
+        host_blocks = self.host_manager.req_to_blocks[request_id]
+        assert host_blocks[page_idx].is_null

+            request_id, page_idx, after_forward=True, require_copy_to_host=True
+        )
+        assert planned
+        state.missing_host_pages.popleft()
+        if not state.missing_host_pages:
+            del self._host_recovery_requests[request_id]
+        self.block_table_updates.add(request_id)
+        return host_block.block_id

issue_comments.body: Thanks for the PR! I think the better approach is to mandate host backing, though, as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59036 does. I'm going to go with that PR and close this one
